featured_reviews.name: Kunjal Karanjavkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst pav bhaji I’ve ever had.
They have “Pav Bhaji Corner” in their name, which makes this even more disappointing. From the look itself, you can tell the quality is completely degraded. There were barely any vegetables in the bhaji, and whatever little chunks were there tasted stale and old.

The pav was no better, had a weird, stale smell and was clearly not fresh. Nothing about this dish felt hygienic or worth the money.

If you’re going to sell pav bhaji, at least get the basics right. This place seriously needs to improve quality, freshness, and standards. Would not recommend at all.

featured_reviews.name: Soniii
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited this restaurant with my friends about a week ago.
We tried the following items:
⭐ Nepali Paneer Chilly – 4/5
⭐ Cheese Pav Bhaji – 3/5
⭐ Veg Cheese Grilled Sandwich – 4/5
⭐ Masala Papad – 4/5
⭐ Mumbai Double Decker Sandwich – 5/5

Overall, the food was okay — some dishes were tasty, especially the Mumbai Double Decker Sandwich which we really loved.

The service was excellent, and the staff was polite and friendly, which made our visit pleasant.

But the most disappointing part was the Dry Fruit Faluda (₹220) — it was too costly and completely tasteless, felt just like plain milk. Definitely not worth the price.

Overall: Average food, excellent service, but very poor dessert quality.

featured_reviews.name: Ashna Bhagtani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We had an absolutely wonderful experience! The dosa was perfectly crisp on the outside and soft inside, served with delicious chutney and flavorful sambar. The pav bhaji was rich, buttery, and full of authentic taste – truly comforting and satisfying.

A very special shout-out to the restaurant team ❤️
We had requested them to prepare the food keeping in mind my elderly mother, who has food tantrums due to her age and is very particular about taste and texture. They were extremely kind and considerate with our request. The food was made just the way she likes it – light, balanced, and easy to eat.

Seeing her enjoy the meal with a big smile meant everything to us. Thank you for your care, patience, and amazing hospitality. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Viren Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ok so everyone has heard about Merwans & I guess most of the people have tried it also.So I would like to share my experience with was pretty average.No doubt the cakes are awesome and pocket friendly, but Merwans also sells secondary eatables like Puffs,Rolls,Breads,Pasteries etc.I spent about a ₹100 and could try atleast 6-7 items, yes you are right 6-7.Starting from the Mini Pizza it was ok you can have one not more than that.Cheese Puff & Vegetable Manchurian Pattice were very average.I mean for ₹12-₹15 I shouldn't expect much still it was merely a pattice without any filling.Though there are few things I liked to, one of them is Pepper Veg Mayonnaise Roll.It was something you should surely try, even the Closed Pizza is good.Coming to Minis try out their Chocolate Square & Mini Dream Chocolate Pastry.There are many more things to try but this was enough to bloat on my stomach.I dint find the place upto the hype, but yeah the place is worth a visit and if you are short with money this is where you should surely hop on to for your mid time hunger.The cakes are awesome and I am a fan of their cakes for sure.
I would like to rate the place as-
Ambience-3
Food-3.5
Service-4
Overall-3.5
Note- You'll should try to increase the filling along with little price hike which would help you increase your customers.This was my view, others may have different opinions.

featured_reviews.name: Rohan Kumbhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Zero. A flatline. An institutional failure masquerading as a store.

​Every visit to Dmart Virar East feels less like shopping and more like an endurance test against utter managerial indifference. This is not just a badly run store; it is a depressing testament to corporate contempt for basic human safety and standards.

​The shelves here are not stocked with fresh products—they are graveyards of the forgotten and the expired. Finding a product within its 'use-by' date is a sad, pathetic lottery. We are constantly forced to sort through mounds of substandard, spoiled, and dangerously expired goods, a clear sign that no one, absolutely no one, who works here gives the slightest damn about what they are selling.

​But the real, crushing hopelessness sets in when you deal with the management. After enduring the grim spectacle of their inventory, you raise a complaint, and what you get back is a black hole of apathy. The management is a complete and utter void. Multiple, desperate attempts to inform them of these health hazards—the mold, the outdated items—have been met with the silent, soul-crushing message: Your health does not matter. Your complaint means nothing.

​It is utterly degrading to spend money here knowing that the very people responsible for your purchase are actively ignoring the risk of selling you something that could make you sick. This branch is a pathetic joke, a miserable failure of retail responsibility, and should be shut down before their negligence actually hospitalizes someone. Avoid this depressing health trap at all costs.
